# Capturefab

> A camera capture command-line tool for people, scripts and AI agents: find, configure, capture from and record GigE Vision, USB3 Vision and GenICam cameras, webcams, RTSP/SRT/ONVIF streams and files, with one JSON document and a typed exit code per command.

Capturefab is one `capturefab` executable for macOS, Windows and Linux. GigE Vision, USB3 Vision and GenICam are implemented natively in Rust (no vendor SDK); webcams, streams, files and video encoding use an FFmpeg executable embedded in every download. The simulator camera `sim:0` lets every command run without hardware. Capturefab is MIT-licensed and has no telemetry.

## For agents

- [Agent instructions](agents.md): rules, permissions, call patterns for common tasks and error recovery by `error.code`.
- [Command reference](reference.html): every command, option, JSON result field, exit code and error code, generated from `capturefab schema`.
- `capturefab schema` prints the same contract as JSON (about 9 KB, roughly 3,000 tokens); `capturefab schema COMMAND` describes one command.

## Contract in brief

- `--json` (or `CAPTUREFAB_JSON=1`): exactly one single-line JSON document on stdout. Exit 0: the result. Non-zero: `{"error":{"code","message","hint"?,"details"?}}`. `watch` and `shell` stream one JSON line per measurement or command instead.
- Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 unavailable, 4 timeout, 5 unsupported, 6 storage full, 130 interrupted.
- Cameras: `-c` takes a `list` ID, serial, IP address, `rtsp://`, `srt://`, `http(s)://`, `onvif://host`, a file path, `sim:N` or `sim:replay:PATH`.
- Names: GenICam features, banks such as `TriggerMode[FrameStart]` (quote them in the shell), and controls `exposure`, `gain`, `fps`, `roi`, `format`, `trigger`, `auto_exposure`, `auto_wb`.
- Durations need a unit (`250ms`, `2s`, `1h30m`); files are never overwritten (`{seq}` in `-o`, or `--on-exists number`).
- Cameras stay open for 60 s between calls in the `auto` session (`--keep 5m` for longer, `--keep 0` or `--no-session` to close at once); `--background` returns a job (`jobs`, `jobs wait`, `jobs stop`).
- Storage full (exit 6) means a write would take the disk below its free-space floor (`CAPTUREFAB_MIN_FREE`).
- Every common PFNC pixel format converts; PNG keeps monochrome wider than 8 bits as 16-bit gray, results report `bit_depth` and `source_bits`, and `-f raw` keeps the exact bytes with a `NAME.json` sidecar. Webcams, streams and files arrive in the format FFmpeg decodes them to (gray, YUV such as `YCbCr709_420_8_Planar`, or RGB8).
- `CAPTUREFAB_JPEG=auto|cpu|videotoolbox` chooses the JPEG encoder and `CAPTUREFAB_HWDEC=auto|none|METHOD` hardware decoding; `doctor --json` reports both (`jpeg`, `hwdec`).

## Common calls

- Find cameras: `capturefab list --json`
- What a camera can do: `capturefab info --json -c CAM`
- Measure exposure and focus: `capturefab inspect --json -c CAM --preview none` (`verdict` is a list; `["ok"]` means well exposed)
- Change settings and measure in one call: `capturefab inspect --json -c CAM --set exposure=5ms`
- Capture: `capturefab capture --json -c CAM -o 'shots/{seq}.png'`
- Time lapse: `capturefab capture --json -c CAM --every 10s --for 1h -o 'lapse/{seq}.jpg' --background`
- Record: `capturefab record --json -c CAM -o clip.mp4 --for 30s`
- Live measurements: `capturefab watch --json -c CAM --for 10s` (one JSON line per measurement)
- Several commands in one start: `capturefab shell --json -c CAM -e 'inspect --preview none' -e 'capture -o shot.png'`
- Check this computer: `capturefab doctor --json`

- [Documentation](docs.html): installation, first capture and task guides.
- [CLI workflows](guides/cli-workflows.md): end-to-end shell recipes.
- [Simulated cameras](guides/simulation.md): `sim:N`, typed simulators and replaying files.
- [Camera compatibility](guides/camera-compatibility.md): transport requirements, pixel formats and known limits.
- [Embedded and read-only hosts](guides/embedded.md): folders, fallbacks and limits on small and immutable systems.
- [Plant-floor capture](guides/plant-floor.md): naming, tags and folders for analysis.
- [Line computers](guides/line-computer.md): sessions under systemd on Raspberry Pi, Jetson and industrial PCs.
- [FFmpeg build and licensing](guides/ffmpeg-build.md): the embedded FFmpeg and its corresponding source.

- [Downloads](downloads.html): archives for every system with SHA-256 checksums.
